title: Volumetric changes in articulating interpositional spacers for two-stage temporomandibular joint arthroplasty. A pilot study
html: Two-stage temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthroplasty may involve the placement of a spacer until a final prosthesis is placed. In cases where a patient is not immobilized via intermaxillary fixation (IMF), the spacer is considered to be articulating, and the patient can open their mouth and function more normally during this interval. This study was designed to retrospectively assess the volumetric changes of the spacer within the temporomandibular joint following the use of an articulating bone cement spacer in a two-stage reconstruction.
